aprende.title: What does it mean?
aprende.intro: The words FarmTwin uses, explained simply.

et.title: Evapotranspiration (ET)
et.text: The water that soil and plants give back to the air: what evaporates plus what the leaves transpire. More sun, wind and dry air mean more water lost.
et.example: Reference ET is around 5 to 6 mm per day: each hectare loses about 50 to 60 m³ of water daily (approximate value).

kc.title: Crop coefficient (Kc)
kc.text: How much water a crop uses compared with a reference grass. It changes with the stage: low at sowing, high at full leaf and lower at maturity.
kc.example: Potato at full leaf has a Kc of 1.15: it uses 15% more water than the reference grass.

ndvi.title: NDVI (greenness)
ndvi.text: An index from 0 to 1 that measures how green and active vegetation is, comparing the red and infrared light it reflects. Near 0 is bare soil; near 1, a dense crop.
ndvi.example: On the map, irrigated fields look green against the brown desert around them.

soilMoisture.title: Soil moisture
soilMoisture.text: How much water there is in the ground, where roots take it up. The SMAP satellite estimates it from space in squares of about 9 km.
soilMoisture.example: Since it hardly rains, moisture depends on irrigation: SMAP shows the regional trend, not your exact field.

waterBalance.title: Water balance
waterBalance.text: The water account: what the crop needs minus the rain it can use. Irrigation covers the rest, and part of it is lost depending on the system.
waterBalance.example: With furrow irrigation about 45% of the water reaches the plant; with drip, about 90%.

frost.title: Frost risk
frost.text: How often the temperature dropped below 0 °C in a given week, counting 20 years of daily minimums. Frost during flowering can ruin a harvest.
frost.example: The coldest nights usually come between June and August.

range.title: Range: good and bad years
range.text: Instead of a single number, FarmTwin shows what happened in real years: the middle value and the range where 8 out of 10 years fell.
range.example: "14,000 m³/ha, range 12,500 – 15,800" means that in 8 out of 10 years the rotation needed between those amounts.

satGround.title: Satellite and ground measurements
satGround.text: Satellites see the whole territory every day but average large areas. A ground station measures precisely, but only at its spot. Together they give coverage and confidence.
satGround.example: That is why NASA POWER weather is checked against a nearby SENAMHI station.
